headline: Iran-US tensions send oil surging past $81 and rattle markets — your portfolio holds steady but watch for RBA rate hike risk building at home.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Biggest mover in today's ASX session, sliding 1.6%. Emerging markets are getting caught in the crossfire of Iran-US tensions — rising oil prices and global risk-off sentiment hit developing economies harder than developed ones. Nothing broken in the long-term thesis; this is geopolitical noise.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 1.5% in last night's US session, bucking the broader NASDAQ sell-off. Investor optimism is building ahead of Microsoft's fiscal Q4 earnings on July 29, with the market betting hard on AI-driven revenue growth from Azure and Copilot products.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced 1.1% today on the ASX. There's growing chatter that lithium stocks may be forming a new uptrend after a brutal few years. Still a deep loss position overall (-32.8%), but today's move is a small positive signal.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 1.2% in last night's session as Wall Street trimmed price targets on big tech ahead of Q2 earnings. The broader NASDAQ was down 1.55%, so Google largely moved with the market. Q2 earnings are coming up — bulls point to expanding TPU (custom chip) sales and strong cloud growth as reasons for optimism.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Slipped about 1% today, dragged by weakness in memory chip stocks overnight — SK Hynix's weak outlook knocked Micron and others down 6%, hurting the AI hardware cohort that this ETF holds. Still down 14.5% overall; the AI theme is real but the ETF has been a rough ride.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Basically flat last night, up 0.37%. No major news. GTA VI hype continues to underpin sentiment around the stock; it's up 6.4% overall in the portfolio.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: A tiny dip of 0.2% today on the ASX, reflecting the softness in US markets overnight. With the S&P 500 down 0.79% last night, this is a very mild tracking move — nothing to worry about.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Essentially flat today — up just 2 cents. VDHG's diversified nature cushioned it nicely from today's volatility. Sits just slightly above your cost basis and doing its job as a steady compounder.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings on July 29 — big moment approaching
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports fiscal Q4 results on July 29 (US time). The market is buzzing — some analysts reckon the stock could 'go parabolic' if Azure AI revenue surprises to the upside. You're currently sitting at an 11.8% loss on MSFT, so this is a genuine catalyst that could swing things. As a long-term holder, just sit tight and let the earnings do the talking.

watch_today.title: GOOG Q2 earnings approaching — bulls optimistic
watch_today.detail: Google's Q2 earnings are also on the horizon. Wall Street trimmed some price targets last night (contributing to the 1.2% dip), but the underlying story looks solid — Google is reportedly expanding sales of its custom TPU chips to battle Nvidia, and cloud growth remains strong. You're up 14% on this position. No reason to change anything.

watch_today.title: Oil up 3.7% — Iran-US conflict risk is real for your hip pocket
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped to US$81 last night as Iran claimed a major drone strike on US military bases in Kuwait, and the US and Iran are increasingly fighting over the Strait of Hormuz (a key shipping chokepoint). ABC News is already flagging fuel rationing fears and petrol price spikes in Australia. This affects everyone at the bowser — worth keeping a close eye on this week.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike risk rising — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: Multiple analysts including Westpac are now flagging the possibility of an Australian interest rate HIKE if the Iran conflict keeps oil prices elevated. New Zealand's central bank has already warned the same. Higher rates would squeeze household budgets and could hurt growth-heavy parts of your portfolio. No action needed today, but this is a genuine risk building this week.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — tough position but a small bounce today
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is still your biggest loss (-32.8%), but it gained 1.1% today and there are early signs lithium stocks may be finding a floor on the ASX. The long-term thesis — lithium demand for EVs — is intact even if the timeline has stretched. Nothing to do here but hold and be patient.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX dipped on emerging market jitters — long-term case unchanged
watch_today.detail: Your emerging markets ETF was the worst performer in today's session, down 1.6%, as geopolitical tension and rising oil prices spook investors in developing economies. This is short-term noise — the long-term case for emerging market exposure (China, India, Southeast Asia growth) hasn't changed. Sit tight.

world.summary: Iran-US military escalation is dominating global headlines, with drone strikes, oil market surges, and fears of a wider Middle East conflict reshaping the economic outlook for everyone.

stories.title: Iran Claims Major Drone Strike on US Military Bases in Kuwait
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has claimed responsibility for a major drone strike on US military bases in Kuwait, marking a sharp escalation in the ongoing US-Iran conflict. This follows ongoing fighting over the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil passes. For everyday Australians, this means higher petrol prices are likely in coming weeks, and global financial markets are jittery.

stories.title: Fuel Rationing and Petrol Price Spike Fears as Iran War Drives Oil Surge
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) jumped 3.7% to US$81 a barrel last night as the Iran-US conflict rattled energy markets. ABC News is reporting fears of fuel rationing and petrol price spikes in Australia. If Iran closes or disrupts the Strait of Hormuz, global oil supply could tighten dramatically — last time this happened, pump prices shot up fast. Australian households and businesses that rely on road transport would feel this directly.

stories.title: US and Iran Vie for the Strait of Hormuz — 1,000 Days of War Reshaping the Middle East
stories.why_it_matters: The SMH reports that the US and Iran are now locked in a battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil shipping lane. Bloomberg notes this conflict has now been running for 1,000 days and has fundamentally reshaped Middle East geopolitics. Iran appears to be betting that the US (and Trump specifically) will eventually back down rather than risk a full-scale war — a dangerous gamble with global consequences.

stories.title: Trump Moves to Tighten Federal Control of US Elections Ahead of Midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is pushing to bring federal elections under greater central government control ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections. This has sparked fierce debate about states' rights and election integrity. For investors, political instability in the US adds another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile environment — midterm elections could shift the balance of power in Congress and affect economic policy.

stories.title: New Zealand Central Bank Warns Middle East Conflict Could Force More Rate Hikes
stories.why_it_matters: New Zealand's Reserve Bank governor has warned that if the Middle East conflict keeps pushing oil prices higher, it could force central banks — including potentially the RBA — to raise interest rates rather than cut them. This is a direct threat to mortgage holders across Australia and New Zealand who've been hoping for rate relief. Higher oil = higher inflation = higher rates = more pain for borrowers.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, the NASDAQ dropped 1.55% and the S&P 500 fell 0.79% as Iran-US tensions and pre-earnings jitters hit big tech. Oil surged 3.7% to US$81, gold hit a fresh high near US$4,025, and the Aussie dollar barely moved. The ASX 200 closed flat today.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Flat close today — the ASX largely shrugged off US weakness overnight, perhaps already pricing in some geopolitical risk.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw the S&P pull back 0.79% as investors digested Iran-US escalation and trimmed risk ahead of big tech earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks bore the brunt last night — NASDAQ fell 1.55% as Wall Street cut price targets on several big tech names ahead of Q2 earnings season.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big move — oil surged 3.7% on Iran-US military escalation and fears over Strait of Hormuz disruption. Expect petrol price rises at the pump soon.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold nudged higher to above US$4,000, reflecting safe-haven demand as geopolitical tensions rise. New record territory.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was essentially unchanged — holding just under 69.5 US cents. Stable for now, but rate hike speculation could shift this.

politics.summary: Australian interest rate expectations are being turned on their head by the Iran-US conflict, with major banks now flagging possible hikes rather than cuts — a big deal for mortgage holders.

stories.title: Westpac Signals Australian Interest Rate Hike Ahead
stories.why_it_matters: Westpac — one of Australia's big four banks — is now signalling that an RBA interest rate hike is possible if oil prices stay elevated due to the Iran-US conflict. This is a significant reversal from the widely-held view just months ago that the next move would be a cut. Higher oil means higher fuel and goods costs, which feeds directly into inflation, making it harder for the RBA to keep rates steady or cut them.

stories.title: Major Bank Drops New Expectation for 2027 Rate Cuts
stories.why_it_matters: A major Australian bank has scrapped its forecast for rate cuts in 2027, reflecting the rapidly changing picture around inflation and global energy prices. Anyone planning their household budget or investment decisions around cheaper borrowing costs in the next few years should take note — that relief may now be pushed out further, or not come at all if the Middle East situation worsens.

stories.title: Australian Interest Rate Hike Likely if US-Iran Conflict Persists — Analysts
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple analysts are now connecting the dots: a prolonged Iran-US conflict keeps oil prices high, which keeps Australian inflation elevated, which forces the RBA to consider hiking rates. The RBA has been on hold after a long tightening cycle — this scenario could mean rates stay higher for even longer. Homeowners on variable rate mortgages are most exposed. Australia's AI regulatory approach is also in the spotlight ahead of a Prime Ministerial speech — more on that in the AI section.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the big theme today — from street protests outside OpenAI and Google's offices, to confusion about how companies should actually comply with a patchwork of new laws worldwide. Meta also launched a new AI model entering the developer market.

stories.title: Protesters March on OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind Demanding AI Development Pause
stories.why_it_matters: Protesters gathered outside the San Francisco offices of OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google DeepMind last night, calling for a pause in AI development until safety standards are established. The demonstrations reflect growing public unease about the pace of AI — particularly around job displacement and the risks of increasingly autonomous systems. It's a sign the political pressure on these companies is building from the street level up.

stories.title: AI Makers Struggling With New AI Laws as Regulations Go Global
stories.why_it_matters: Forbes reports that AI companies are struggling to comply with a chaotic patchwork of new AI laws — the EU has its AI Act, the US has state-by-state rules, and now Australia is considering its own approach. Companies like Google, Microsoft and Meta are having to shape their AI chatbots differently depending on what country they're operating in. This adds real compliance costs and could slow the rollout of new AI features — relevant to any investor holding these stocks.

stories.title: Australia's AI Regulatory Approach in Focus Ahead of PM's Speech
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian PM is set to give a major speech on AI regulation, with the country's approach being closely watched by the tech industry. Australia has so far taken a lighter-touch, principles-based approach — meaning companies get more flexibility but also less certainty. The Lowy Institute argues that current AI regulation globally is 'answering the wrong question,' focusing too much on controlling the technology rather than building the capability to use it well.

stories.title: Meta Launches Muse Spark 1.1 AI Model, Enters Developer API Market
stories.why_it_matters: Meta (Facebook's parent company) has launched a new AI model called Muse Spark 1.1 and is now entering the developer API market — meaning it's opening its AI up for other companies to build products on top of. This puts Meta in direct competition with OpenAI's ChatGPT API and Google's Gemini API. More competition in this space generally means lower prices and better tools for businesses, and signals that the AI race is far from settled.

sport.summary: NRL Round 20 kicks off Thursday with Panthers vs Broncos. Cruz Hewitt — Lleyton's son — had Wimbledon heartbreak but is targeting the Australian Open. AFL finals picture is clarifying with some big clubs set to miss out.

stories.title: Warriors vs Dragons Round 20: Origin Stars Return, Valentine Suli Recalled
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors will have a boosted lineup for their Saturday clash against the Dragons, with State of Origin representatives returning to the side and Valentine Suli recalled. It's shaping up as a competitive match — the Warriors are looking to consolidate their top-eight spot while the Dragons are on an active recruitment drive but still rebuilding on the field.

stories.title: Round 20 Team Lists: Every Club's Confirmed Lineup
stories.why_it_matters: All Round 20 team lists are confirmed. Key matchups include Panthers vs Broncos (Thursday night), Roosters vs Storm (Friday night), and the local Gold Coast derby — Titans vs Sea Eagles on Sunday at Cbus Super Stadium at 2pm. The Titans have named a settled lineup under coach Hannay for the Sea Eagles showdown.

stories.title: Cruz Hewitt Targets Australian Open After Wimbledon Boys' Final Heartbreak
stories.why_it_matters: Cruz Hewitt, 17-year-old son of Aussie tennis legend Lleyton Hewitt, lost the Wimbledon Boys' Final in heartbreaking fashion — his final junior tournament before turning professional. Cruz has set his sights on playing the Australian Open in January, where he'd compete for the first time at a senior Grand Slam on home soil. A real feel-good Aussie story to watch unfold.

stories.title: AFL Ladder Predictor: Collingwood and Carlton Set to Miss Finals, Top Four Locked In
stories.why_it_matters: AFL.com.au's ladder predictor is showing Collingwood (the reigning premiers) and Carlton are both in danger of missing the finals entirely — a massive shock for two of the competition's biggest clubs. The top four is reportedly locked in, meaning the battle for spots 5-8 will be intense over the remaining rounds. Big news for footy fans heading into the business end of the season.

stories.title: Jarome Luai Rugby League Switch Rumours Surface — Craig Cronk Floats Surprise Move
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports reports that rugby league great Cooper Cronk has floated the idea of Panthers star Jarome Luai potentially making a shock move to rugby union. Luai is one of the NRL's most exciting players and is off-contract — any switch to the 15-man code would be a major story. Nothing confirmed, but it's the kind of rumour that tends to build legs quickly.
